title: Trump Sues ABC News for $10 Billion Over Ross Reporting Error
description_short: Trump Sues ABC News for $10 Billion Over Ross Reporting Error
description_medium: On March 18, 2024, Donald Trump sued ABC News and anchor George Stephanopoulos over a statement made during an interview about the civil verdict in E. Jean Carroll’s case. Trump alleged that the broadcast misstated the verdict and sought $10 billion in damages. The filing records his claim; it does not establish that the network acted with the legally required fault.
description_long: Trump filed a defamation lawsuit against ABC News and George Stephanopoulos on March 18, 2024, after the anchor said during an interview that Trump had been found liable for rape in the civil case brought by E. Jean Carroll. The jury had found Trump liable for sexual abuse, not rape, and the lawsuit argued that the distinction made the broadcast defamatory. Trump sought $10 billion in damages. Those details describe the allegation in the filing, not a court finding that ABC was liable or that the requested amount reflected proven harm. The source linked for this entry is an account of the lawsuit when it was filed; it does not document later developments. Any correction, settlement, or final disposition would require a separate source and is not included here. The case raised a dispute about how news organizations describe a civil verdict and how a public figure may seek redress for an allegedly false statement. The record does not establish that the suit was intended to intimidate the press, so no motive is assigned.
